## What I wrote

`tests/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVPrinterAgentTest.java` — a self-contained JUnit 3.8 test class (`extends junit.framework.TestCase`, no annotations, no external helpers), matching the JUnit version in `lib/` and compiling cleanly under `-source 8`.

### Approach
The only `CSVFormat` member the javadoc actually exposes is `CSVFormat.DEFAULT` (via the package-summary example `CSVFormat.DEFAULT.parse(in)`), so every expectation is built against that RFC 4180 dialect: `,` delimiter, `"` quote (doubled inside values), `\r\n` record separator, comments disabled.

### Coverage (30 tests)
- **Constructor / `getOut()`**: returns the same `Appendable`; headerless format writes nothing on construction; `IllegalArgumentException` for null `out` and null `format` (documented).
- **`print`**: value written with no leading separator; delimiter inserted before every value except the first; plain values unquoted; encapsulation for values containing the delimiter, the quote char (with doubling), LF, and CR; non-String rendered via `toString`.
- **`println`**: emits `\r\n`; consecutive calls make blank records; only `println` terminates a record; starting a new record suppresses the leading delimiter.
- **`printRecord(Object...)` / `(Iterable)`**: one terminated line; selective quoting; empty args → just the separator; interior empty fields preserved; lone empty field encapsulated as `""` (round-trip rationale); null value → empty field; mixed object types; successive calls accumulate; `print` after `printRecord` continues on the next line.
- **`printRecords(Object[])` / `(Iterable)` / `(ResultSet)`**: one record per element; empty input writes nothing; ResultSet fixture (inline `java.lang.reflect.Proxy`, no mock library) writes every row and nothing for zero rows.
- **`printComment`**: no output when comments are disabled (DEFAULT); doesn't disturb surrounding records.
- **`flush` / `close`**: forwarded to the underlying stream — verified with an inline `TrackingWriter extends Writer` that counts calls and captures written text.

Boundary/error cases (nulls, empty inputs, special characters, zero-row result set) are asserted on observable output/state, not just absence of exceptions. Lower-certainty points where the javadoc is silent (null rendering, lone-empty-field quoting, close propagation) are asserted to the contract-implied behavior with an explanatory comment.
